purpose: Build an adaptive opponent AI engine for a WebXR table tennis game with three distinct difficulty levels that feel architecturally different, not just numerically tuned.

tech_stack.version_constraint: three@^0.170.0 or newer with WebGPURenderer support
do_not_use: WebGL fallback (project is WebGPU-only; show upgrade message on unsupported browsers)
setInterval or setTimeout for game loop timing (use xrSession.requestAnimationFrame deltas)
localStorage / sessionStorage inside the engine module (host app handles persistence)

deployment_requirements.cross_origin_isolation: Server MUST send Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin AND Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp headers. Without these, SharedArrayBuffer is disabled and worker comms fall back to slow postMessage copies. Document this in README and provide a vite.config.ts that sets these headers in dev server.

responsibilities: Input event capture (controller pose, paddle pose, ball-paddle collision events)
Shot event logging (postMessage to AI worker)
Reading AI target coordinates (postMessage from AI worker)
forbidden_operations: Clustering or statistical math beyond simple arithmetic

physics_worker.sync_mechanism: SharedArrayBuffer with Atomics for ball state (position xyz, velocity xyz, spin xyz, timestamp). 32 bytes total, lock-free read on main thread.

ai_worker.must_not: Block on rendering or read DOM

engine/.TableTennisEngine.ts: Public API: init(), startMatch(difficulty), onShot(), getAITarget()
engine/.PhysicsBridge.ts: Owns physics worker, reads ball state via SAB
engine/.AIBridge.ts: Owns AI worker, sends shot events, receives targets

ai/.worker.ts: AI worker entry point with message router

engines/.IAIEngine.ts: Interface: ingestShot(shot), computeTarget(context) => {x, z, confidence}, reset()
engines/.BeginnerEngine.ts: Pure random within safe zones, no learning
engines/.ProEngine.ts: LSTM via tfjs-webgpu + Voronoi fallback when confidence < 0.4

models/.shot_predictor_lstm.json: Pre-trained tfjs model (host app provides; engine loads at startMatch if difficulty=pro)
models/.README.md: Document expected input shape [batch=1, timesteps=20, features=6] and output [x, z, confidence]

rendering/.Table.ts: Standard ITTF table dimensions: 2.74m x 1.525m x 0.76m (length x width x height)
rendering/.BallTrail.ts: GPU-instanced particle trail (optional, can be disabled on Quest 2)

input/.PaddleTracker.ts: Read controller or hand pose, smooth with one-euro filter (cutoff=1.0, beta=0.007) to kill jitter without adding lag

shot_event_schema.description: Every time the player's paddle contacts the ball, main thread emits this to AI worker.

fields.landing_x: float32, meters from table center, range [-0.7625, 0.7625]
fields.landing_z: float32, meters from net on player side, range [0, 1.37]
fields.success: 0 or 1, did the player return it cleanly (no double-bounce, no out)
fields.swing_lateness_ms: float32, time between ball-crossing-net and paddle contact. Positive = late, negative = early.
fields.ball_spin_rps: float32, revolutions per second around vertical axis (signed)

shot_event_schema.encoding: Float32Array of length 8, transferred via postMessage transferable

ai_target_schema.description: AI worker returns this when main thread requests next target.

fields.target_x: float32, meters from table center on PLAYER side, range [-0.7, 0.7] (0.0625m safety margin from edge)
fields.target_z: float32, meters from net on player side, range [0.1, 1.3]
fields.confidence: float32, range [0, 1], used for hybrid fallback decisions

beginner.behavior: Aims at center 60% of player side with Gaussian jitter sigma=0.25m. Never targets corners. Ball speed 3-5 m/s. Minimal spin (-5 to 5 rps). No learning. Feels like a patient practice partner.
beginner.miss_rate_target: Player should win ~80% of rallies in first session

intermediate.behavior: Voronoi heatmap over last 15 shots. Struggle score = (misses * 3) + (lateness_ms / 100 * 2) + (successes * 0.5). Decay multiplier 0.93 per rally. Min 5 shots before exploit activates. Exploit factor 0.5 (50% targets weak zones, 50% random). Cell area floor 0.015 sqm. Bayesian shrinkage with prior n=3 on per-cell scores.
intermediate.miss_rate_target: Player should win ~50% of rallies after 10 sessions

pro.behavior: LSTM trained on shot sequences predicts player return position with 200ms lookahead. Input: last 20 shots (sequence of 6-feature vectors). Output: predicted (x, z, confidence). If confidence >= 0.4, AI targets the OPPOSITE side of the predicted return (anticipate-and-counter). If confidence < 0.4, fall back to IntermediateEngine logic. Exploit factor 0.85. Adds disguised serves (paddle motion suggests one spin, ball receives different spin via late wrist rotation animation).
pro.miss_rate_target: Player should win ~20% of rallies; should feel like the AI is reading them

performance_budgets.notes: AI target must be requested at least 200ms before the AI paddle swing because postMessage is async and there is no guarantee a worker response lands before the next XR frame. Build this lead time into the rally state machine.

accuracy_guardrails.rationale_grid_snap: Hand-tracking jitter is ~5-10cm. Snap logged coordinates to 10cm grid BEFORE clustering to kill false signal.
accuracy_guardrails.rationale_min_shots: Below 5 samples, the heatmap is statistical noise. AI plays neutral center-table until threshold is reached.
accuracy_guardrails.rationale_min_cell: Cells smaller than 15 cm^2 represent physically meaningless targets given paddle size and ball diameter. Merge with nearest neighbor.
accuracy_guardrails.rationale_shrinkage: Regress low-sample cells toward population mean to prevent overreaction to one unlucky miss.
accuracy_guardrails.rationale_jitter: Add Gaussian jitter to chosen target so AI never hits the same coordinate twice. Without this, players spot the pattern within 5 rallies.

psychological_design_rules.no_heatmap_visualization: Under NO circumstances render the Voronoi grid, struggle scores, or AI targeting logic visibly in the game UI. The system's power is psychological. A debug overlay is allowed but must be gated behind a build flag and OFF in production builds.
psychological_design_rules.no_telegraphed_targeting: AI paddle animation must NOT pre-orient toward the target before swing windup begins. Targeting decision happens during windup, not before.
psychological_design_rules.natural_imperfection: At every difficulty, inject a small random miss-rate (Beginner 15%, Intermediate 8%, Pro 3%). A perfect-precision AI feels like a bot. A slightly fallible one feels human.
psychological_design_rules.no_instant_punishment: When a new player weakness is detected, do NOT exploit on the very next shot. Wait 1-2 rallies. This makes the adaptation feel like recognition, not surveillance.

webxr_specific_requirements.render_loop: Use xrSession.requestAnimationFrame ONLY. Never window.requestAnimationFrame inside an XR session.
webxr_specific_requirements.frame_timing: Use the XRFrame predictedDisplayTime, not performance.now(), for any rendering-related timing.
webxr_specific_requirements.webxr_layers: Use XRQuadLayer for score display and menu UI. These update on-demand, not per-frame, freeing render budget.
webxr_specific_requirements.fixed_foveated_rendering: Enable FFR level 2 on Quest devices via gl.getExtension or WebGPU equivalent.
webxr_specific_requirements.multiview_rendering: Enable WebXR multiview to halve draw calls for stereo rendering.
webxr_specific_requirements.hand_tracking_fallback: If session has hand-tracking input, use it; otherwise use controllers. Code must support both without runtime branching in the hot path.
webxr_specific_requirements.passthrough_mode: If session is immersive-ar (Quest 3 / Vision Pro MR), use scene understanding to anchor table to a real surface. Fall back to floating table if no plane detected within 3s.

methods.init(canvas: HTMLCanvasElement): Promise: Boot WebGPU, spawn workers, load XR session
methods.startMatch(difficulty: 'beginner' | 'int: Reset state, load appropriate AI engine, begin rally state machine
methods.endMatch(): MatchStats: Returns rally count, player win rate, avg rally length, exploit success rate
methods.destroy(): Promise<void>: Terminate workers, dispose GPU resources, end XR session

must_cover: ShotHistory ring buffer wraps correctly at capacity
Decay function applied per rally produces expected weights at t+5, t+10, t+20
Voronoi cell area floor merges sub-threshold cells
Bayesian shrinkage formula on synthetic data matches reference values
Weighted CDF sampling distribution matches input weights within 5% over 10k samples
Grid snap rounds correctly at boundary values
LSTM input normalization produces values in [-1, 1]
Confidence fallback triggers at exactly 0.4 threshold
Full rally completes in beginner mode without errors
AI worker responds to shot events within 5ms
Frame rate stays >= 72fps during 100-rally session on simulated Quest 2 profile

must_measure: p50 and p99 of ai_worker_per_shot_ms across 1000 simulated shots per difficulty
Main thread frame time histogram during 5-minute Pro mode session
GPU memory growth over 30-minute session (must be flat, no leaks)

manual_qa_checklist: Beginner mode: new player wins majority of rallies
Intermediate mode: AI visibly shifts targeting after player consistently fails in one zone
Pro mode: AI appears to anticipate returns (qualitative subjective test with 3 testers)
No debug overlays visible in production build
FPS counter shows >= 72 throughout a 10-minute Pro match on Quest 3

phase_1_foundation: WebXR session boot with controller and hand-tracking support
Table, paddle, ball meshes at correct ITTF dimensions
COOP/COEP headers configured in dev server
phase_2_physics: Rapier physics worker with SharedArrayBuffer ball state
Paddle-ball collision detection on main thread reading SAB
Ball trajectory matches real table tennis physics (verify with reference video)
phase_3_ai_scaffold: End-to-end shot event flow main -> ai_worker -> target -> main
phase_4_intermediate: All accuracy guardrails (grid snap, min cell area, Bayesian shrinkage)
phase_6_polish: Psychological design rules (no telegraphing, natural imperfection, delayed exploitation)
Passthrough mode for Quest 3 / Vision Pro
Performance test suite passes all budgets

non_negotiable_rules: No main-thread math beyond shot logging and target reading.
No WebGL fallback - WebGPU is the floor.
No visible heatmap in production - the AI's intelligence must remain implicit.
No hardcoded magic numbers - all tunables in config files exposed via EngineConfig.
No telemetry or analytics phoning home from the engine module - host app owns that.
No third-party CDN dependencies at runtime - bundle everything.
Each difficulty level must feel architecturally different to a tester, not just numerically different.
deliverables: README.md with setup, build, and deployment instructions
ARCHITECTURE.md explaining the thread model and AI design decisions
Test suite covering unit, integration, and performance requirements
Example index.html that boots the engine and starts a match
